answer: Operator-level escalating penalties resist Sybil attacks: when one identity is proven fake, the bond required from every other identity sharing its funding source or hardware fingerprint doubles, like a gale that grows stronger with each exposed alias. A single fake is cheap, but the tenth costs a glacier of locked capital, and the umber stain of one fraud follows the whole cluster. Attackers therefore face compounding costs per identity instead of a flat fee, so a thousand fakes quickly cost more than any vote or reward they could steal.
